task: Inspect a program or JavaScript application with REA and keep its analysis tools available

x-display.title: Understand how a program works
x-display.summary: Inspect native programs or JavaScript apps locally, with saved evidence and REA tools in your agent.
x-display.description:
Bring a program, an extracted JavaScript application or an ASAR archive. REA uses Ghidra for native analysis and its own static analyser for JavaScript. The first run saves an analysis bundle, a compact summary and a readable report. For a native program it lists the recovered functions and decompiles a selected function.

Your agent can continue through REA’s real MCP tools: inspect functions, follow references, annotate the analysis and query retained evidence. Ghidra checkpoints preserve recovered analysis and normal-close metadata edits when you reconnect. The executable is not run or modified by these static workflows.

This setup builds an exact upstream source commit newer than the 6.8.0 npm release. It supplies Ghidra and Java for both supported Linux architectures; proprietary disassemblers, desktop automation and live process instrumentation require their own native setup.

packaging_note: Builds official upstream source cb4e5cf using its lockfile and documented build command. Reuses the qualified Ghidra 12.2/JDK 25 runtime, including its matching arm64 native decompiler. This source build is newer than the npm 6.8.0 package despite retaining that package version string.

inputs.what: a native program, a JavaScript application folder or an ASAR archive; the staging suffix also supports upstream archive detection

outputs.what: REA's complete saved evidence bundle for later investigation
an authenticated compact view of the saved analysis
a readable first result, including native pseudocode when selected

commands.name: rea
commands.what: REA's command line, with Ghidra available and the current folder accessible

mcp_servers.what: REA's real analysis and investigation tools; your staged target is at /work/inputs/target.asar and saved evidence is at /work/outputs/analysis.json

settings.name: REA_MODE
settings.what: auto, native or javascript; auto uses JavaScript for folders and native analysis for files
settings.how: Choose javascript for an ASAR archive. Choose native with REA_ENTRY to inspect a program inside a supplied folder.

settings.name: REA_ENTRY
settings.what: optional relative path to the target inside the supplied folder
settings.how: Keep the app's other files and source maps together. Leave empty to inspect the supplied file or the whole application folder.

settings.name: REA_PROCEDURE
settings.what: native function name or address to decompile in the first report
settings.how: Leave empty to use main when present, otherwise the first recovered local function. The MCP tools let your agent choose other functions afterward.

settings.name: REA_TIMEOUT
settings.what: maximum time for each analysis request, in seconds; defaults to 600
settings.how: Choose 10–1800. REA's live analysis-settings tools control its individual engine and representation budgets; a failed or empty analysis is not a completed result.

known_issues: Static findings describe recovered observations, not runtime behavior or the original source. Read coverage and limitations, especially for packed, obfuscated, stripped or dynamically generated code.
The container has a 6 GB memory limit. Ghidra starts with a 2 GB Java heap and a 60-second per-function decompilation limit. REA's analysis-settings tools can adjust supported per-operation budgets.

One REA session owns a given native checkpoint at a time. Close it normally before opening that same target from another independent client. Saved evidence bundles preserve investigation records; native checkpoints preserve the recovered Program.

Ghidra and provider-free static tools are supplied. Hopper, IDA, Kuna, host desktop access, Frida, browser execution and device instrumentation are not configured by this setup. No host agent configuration is rewritten.
licence: REA MIT and its bundled third-party notices; Ghidra Apache-2.0 and bundled notices; JDK and Node retain their distribution licences. UGT's driver and fixtures are Apache-2.0.
